# U15 — visible pixel screenshot from REAL Ubuntu ARM64 Wayland (VM ONLY)

**GOAL: produce a genuine pixel screenshot generated by a QEMU ARM64
Ubuntu 26.04 Labwc session, rather than an invented image or a socket-only
handshake. NOT a Pixel 8 GUI release.**

## Basis

- U14 [run #8](https://github.com/TeamWearFreedomProject/Pixel8_Drodian/actions/runs/38067190650) established a real Labwc 0.9.3 compositor, pixman headless backend, 1280x720 software output and actual client registry response.
- U6 original Ubuntu 26.04 ARM64 ext4 rootfs SHA256
  `d3cbe5e0a0e170e9e1e3071b32394e0ddd686887351ed1f4aa2b8bed814bde9e`
  is **read-only and never mutated**.
- U8 and U9 guarded initramfs and generic Linux 6.6.89 **QEMU-only**
  kernel are SHA256-pinned from successful earlier releases.

## U15 graphical pixel generation strategy

- Use the tested **Labwc headless/Pixman** Wayland compositor and start
  the preinstalled ARM64 **Waybar** panel. Its VM-only JSON/CSS config paints
  cyan, blue, magenta and yellow panels, making real pixel differences
  measurable.
- Obtain the **ARM64 grim Wayland screencopy client** from Ubuntu package
  metadata on the runner, and put only that executable in a temporary U6
  ext4 copy. Never install it to the user's Pixel 8.
- Launch a QEMU ARM64 virtual guest and a **separate 64 MiB writable virtual
  ext4 scratch disk**; keep Ubuntu rootfs mounted read-only.
- Connect `grim` to the existing Labwc Wayland socket. Its screenshot
  protocol must export a **real PNG** to the scratch image. The host uses
  read-only `debugfs` extraction of just the PNG.
- PIL checks PNG format, minimum 640x480 dimensions, more than one sampled
  pixel color, and a measurable color difference between the Waybar top panel
  and the lower screen.
- Include the **actual PNG** in a small GitHub Actions artifact, with
  guest serial, pixel statistics, kernel/source hashes and warnings.
- **Do not call this a virtio-gpu output, guest visible VGA screen, native
  DRM connector or real Pixel 8 panel.** The screenshot is from the
  compositor's virtual headless output. A physical/virtio-GPU screen is a
  separate subsequent experiment.

## CI / scripts

- [U15 action](.github/workflows/phase-u15-wayland-pixels-vm.yml)
- [Wayland screenshot guest](scripts/u15_gui_capture_vm.sh)
- [Disposable rootfs preparation and colored Waybar config](scripts/u15_prepare_gui_vm.py)
- [Strict screenshot pixel verifier](scripts/u15_assert_pixels.py)

Do not interpret a test failure as corruption of the user's Pixel 8.
No fastboot, ADB, flashing, actual device access, Android partition mount
or boot image is involved in this workflow. No unverified Pixel 8 boot
procedure is created.

**This commit launches U15 run #1. GUI screen on the real Pixel 8: UNVERIFIED.**

## Retry #2 — ARM64 Ubuntu package repository fix

- [First U15 attempt](https://github.com/TeamWearFreedomProject/Pixel8_Drodian/actions/runs/38087630867) failed before VM boot: after enabling arm64 the runner tried its default `security.ubuntu.com` mirror for ARM64 package indexes, causing HTTP 404. No PNG was produced.
- Corrective change: update only the explicitly configured `ports.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-ports` ARM64 apt source for the screenshot client. No kernel/phone operation and no firmware produced.
- This doc commit starts retry #2. Pixel test remains QEMU headless screencopy only.

## Retry #3 — read-only virtual scratch workaround

- [U15 retry #2](https://github.com/TeamWearFreedomProject/Pixel8_Drodian/actions/runs/38087724563) successfully installed the ARM64 screenshot utility, built the VM copy, and reached real Labwc Wayland protocol handshake.
- Waybar was launched and the `grim` capture command ran, but the separate QEMU virtual scratch ext4 unexpectedly behaved **read-only** and grim reported `Failed to open file ... Read-only file system`. No PNG screenshot was saved, so the job correctly failed.
- U15 now writes the real `grim` screenshot to the existing **writable /run RAM filesystem** inside the guest. A bounded base64 block with explicit markers transfers those original PNG bytes over serial. [Host PNG recovery script](scripts/u15_recover_serial_png.py) reconstructs the actual screenshot, and the pixel verifier still demands nonuniform image content.
- Optional Waybar launch uses `dbus-run-session` where available to avoid D-Bus autolaunch errors in the service environment.
- This document edit starts U15 retry #3. No real phone, Android partitions, or kernel/boot flashing.
